title: Make save() write the output file atomically
description:
## Problem

`XCDESaveEditor._ensure_backup()` writes atomically (temp file + `os.replace`), but `save()` writes the final output file directly with `open(output_path, "wb")`. A crash or disk-full mid-write can leave a truncated/corrupted output file, which the user might then copy over their real save.

## Fix

Apply the same temp + `os.replace` pattern in `save()`. Ensure the temp file is cleaned up on failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `save()` writes via temp file then atomic rename
- [ ] Temp file removed if write fails
- [ ] Unit test verifying output path gets complete data (and no stray temp files remain)

title: Accept character names (not just IDs) in CLI commands
description:
## Background

Commands require numeric character IDs (1-15), forcing users to consult the README table. Error-prone for casual users.

## Proposal

- Accept case-insensitive names everywhere a character ID is accepted: `set-level shulk 99`, `set-ap reyn 99999`
- Custom argparse `type=` that maps name → ID via the `Character` enum
- Keep accepting numeric IDs; update README and CLI epilog

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both name and numeric ID work for all character arguments
- [ ] Unknown names produce a clear error listing valid names
- [ ] Unit tests for the type converter

title: Research whether saves have a checksum; implement fix-up if so
description:
## Question

Does the XCDE save format contain a checksum/hash over the save data (header or trailer), and does the game validate it?

README currently warns "This editor doesn't modify checksums (if any exist)". If one exists and is enforced, edits may be rejected or silently ignored on console (CFW) — resolving this is what would make the editor safe beyond emulators.

## Tasks

- Inspect header/footer bytes of real saves for length/hash-like fields
- Flip a byte in a known field on a copy, load in emulator: accepted or rejected?
- If found: document the algorithm and implement fix-up on write

## Notes

The XCDESave C# library is the primary reference here.

title: Extract duplicated art-unlock validation into a shared helper
description:
## Problem

`set_art_max_unlock()` and `set_all_arts_max_unlock()` each contain near-identical enum/int normalization + bounds checking for the unlock value. The logic is subtly different between them (one checks bounds only in the `int` branch), which invites bugs.

## Fix

Extract a helper, e.g.:

```python
def _normalize_unlock_value(self, value):
    """Accept int (0-3) or ArtsLevelUnlocked; return int, raise ValueError otherwise."""
```

and use it in both setters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single shared validation path for both methods
- [ ] Existing tests still pass; add tests for enum input and out-of-range input on both setters

title: Add diff command to compare two save files
description:
## Background

Reverse-engineering new save structures (SP, inventory, gems, completion flags...) currently has no tooling support. Locating "which bytes changed after performing an in-game action" requires manual hex comparison, which is tedious and error-prone.

## Proposal

Add a `diff` subcommand:

```
python xcde_editor.py diff <save1> <save2> [--hex] [--gap N]
```

- Report all differing byte ranges; regions closer than `--gap` bytes (default ~8) are merged into one region
- Annotate output with known field labels (party member blocks: level/XP/AP; arts table; money offset) so users immediately recognize known vs. unknown regions
- `--hex` prints a hex dump of each differing region (old vs. new)
- Validate both files with the existing save validation logic

## Value

This is the enabler for all "new offset" issues (SP, inventory, gems, etc.): save before/after an in-game action, diff, and the changed offsets surface immediately. Also useful for users to verify what an edit actually changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Diffing two identical files reports "no differences" and exits 0
- [ ] Diffing a modified save lists regions, with known offsets labeled
- [ ] `--hex` shows before/after hex dumps per region
- [ ] Unit tests cover merged-region logic and known-field labeling using fabricated saves

title: Epic: extend editor coverage to more save structures (SP, inventory, gems, completion)
description:
## Goal

Extend the editor beyond the currently supported fields (level/XP/AP, arts levels & unlock, money) to cover the game's major systems. Each child issue targets one system and requires reverse-engineering its offsets in the save file.

## Approach

Use the `diff` command (see dependency) on before/after saves to locate candidate offsets, then cross-check against the damysteryman/XCDESave C# library structures and real saves before hardcoding offsets.

## Ground rules for children

- New offsets must be validated on real save files, not just fabricated data
- Follow existing patterns: constants on the editor class, bounded setters with validation, subcommand + alias, unit tests
- Prefer `get_*`/`set_*` + a `set-all` variant where it makes sense

## Children

- SP & skill trees
- Inventory items (materials count, add weapons/armor)
- Crystals & gems
- Collectopaedia completion
- Colony 6 reconstruction
- Fashion outfits (DE costume system)
- Play time
- Noponstones (Time Attack currency)

title: Add SP / skill tree editing
description:
## Target

Skill Points (SP) and the skill tree system: per-character SP amount, skill tree unlock/progression, learned skills.

## Tasks

- Reverse-engineer SP + skill tree offsets (member block or separate tables) using the diff command and XCDESave C# library
- `get/set-sp`, unlock skill trees, learn all skills per tree
- Likely a `set-all-sp` + "learn all skills" bulk command

## Notes

Skill trees are a core progression system; expected high demand. The party member block (0x138 bytes each) has unexplored regions that may contain some of this data.

title: Add inventory item viewing/editing
description:
## Target

Inventory: materials/sellables with counts, key items; adding weapons and armor (including unobtained rares).

## Tasks

- Reverse-engineer the item list structure (likely item-ID + count arrays) via diff command + XCDESave library
- `list-items`, `set-item-count <id> <count>`, `add-item <id> [count]`
- Equipment add/modify if structure permits (slots, gems)

## Notes

Inventory structures are usually the most complex part of save formats; expect count-prefixed arrays rather than fixed offsets. Start read-only (`list-items`) before attempting writes.

title: Add crystal/gem editing
description:
## Target

Crystals (unrefined) and crafted gems: view, modify stats, or directly insert max-tier gems (e.g. perfect "Attack V"-style gems) without the crafting minigame.

## Tasks

- Reverse-engineer crystal/gem inventory structures (likely ID + attribute data) via diff command + XCDESave library
- `list-gems`, `add-gem <template>` with a small table of popular max gems
- Crystal heat/quality fields if present

## Notes

Gem crafting is one of the grindiest systems in the game; a "insert perfect gems" feature is a headline use case for the editor.

title: Add play time editing
description:
## Target

Play time counter in the save header.

## Tasks

- Locate play time field (header area, 0x00-0x100 region of the file; format likely seconds or h/m/s packed)
- `get/set-playtime` with sane bounds (0..999:59:59)
- Method: create save, wait a known duration in-game (or use two saves with known time difference), diff

title: Add Noponstones (Time Attack currency) editing
description:
## Target

Noponstones, the DE Time Attack mode currency used to buy fashion/gems/arts boosts.

## Tasks

- Locate the counter (likely near money or in a Time Attack section)
- `get/set-noponstones` with bounds validation

title: Add collectopaedia completion
description:
## Target

Collectopaedia completion: mark all entries as collected for each region.

## Tasks

- Locate collectopaedia bitmask/array (likely region-wise bitfields)
- `collect-all` command to set everything collected (includes the reward-claiming implications — investigate whether rewards are granted retroactively or flagged separately)

title: Add Colony 6 reconstruction editing
description:
## Target

Colony 6 reconstruction: immigrant counts per category and reconstruction level (special/mining/nature/housing stages).

## Tasks

- Locate reconstruction state (levels + recruited immigrant counts)
- `set-colony6 <level>` to set reconstruction stage and fill immigrant slots
- Verify on a real save mid-reconstruction

title: Add fashion outfit unlock-all
description:
## Target

DE-exclusive fashion/costume system: unlock all outfits for all characters without farming Time Attack.

## Tasks

- Locate unlocked fashion items list (probably a bitmask or ID array)
- `unlock-all-fashion` command

title: Add --in-place option to overwrite the original save file
description:
## Background

Emulator users must keep the exact save filename (`bfsgame00.sav`); currently the editor only writes `<file>.modified` and the user renames manually. This is a common friction point.

## Proposal

Add `--in-place` (global + per-subcommand, like `--dry-run`):

- Writes to the original path instead of `.modified`
- Must succeed at creating a backup first; if backup creation fails, abort without touching the original
- Plays nicely with `--dry-run` (prints what would be written)
- `restore-backup` (separate issue) pairs with this for rollback

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--in-place` overwrites the original only after a successful backup
- [ ] Backup failure leaves the original untouched
- [ ] Tests cover in-place write + backup interaction

title: Add incremental commands (add-money / add-ap / add-xp)
description:
## Background

All current setters overwrite with an absolute value. Accidentally setting money/AP to a typo'd value destroys the original with no undo.

## Proposal

- `add-money <amount>`: add (or subtract with negative values) to current gold, clamped to 0..MAX_MONEY_VALUE
- `add-ap <character_id> <amount>`: same for a character's AP
- Optionally `add-xp <character_id> <amount>`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Negative deltas clamp at 0 instead of raising or wrapping
- [ ] Overflow clamps at the max instead of wrapping
- [ ] Unit tests for clamping behavior

title: Add interactive menu mode (-i)
description:
## Target

Menu-driven interactive mode: `python xcde_editor.py -i <save>` shows stats and a menu loop (view / edit characters / arts / money / save & exit).

## Value

Lowers the barrier for non-CLI users; natural frontend once more fields are supported.

## Notes

Keep it dependency-free (plain input() loop). Only worth building after the command set stabilizes (new-fields epic), to avoid reworking menus repeatedly.

title: Add JSON export/import for all known fields
description:
## Target

Round-trip JSON export/import:

- `export-json <save> <out.json>`: dump all known fields (characters, arts, money, future fields) to readable JSON
- `import-json <save> <in.json>`: apply values back with full validation

## Value

- Users can hand-edit many fields in one pass instead of chaining CLI commands
- Future field additions become usable without CLI changes
- Provides a clean machine interface for other tools/frontends

## Notes

Design the schema versioned (e.g. `"format": 1`) and reject unknown/missing keys explicitly. Depends conceptually on the field coverage of the new-structures epic but can ship with current fields already.

title: Add max-out one-click command
description:
## Background

The most common request for a save editor is "make my save maxed". Today that requires chaining 4 commands.

## Proposal

`max-out` (alias `mo`):

- All characters to level 99
- All AP set to a high value (e.g. 99999) — all characters, so arts can be maxed in-game
- Money to max
- All arts to level 12 with max unlock tier 3 (XII_MASTER)

Document in README with a warning about spoilers/difficulty.

## Dependencies

Builds on `set-all-ap`/`set-all-xp` (batch setters).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single command applies all of the above
- [ ] `--dry-run` previews every change
- [ ] Unit test verifying each affected offset after running

title: Add per-art editing (get-art/set-art/list-arts with art names)
description:
## Background

Arts can currently only be bulk-modified (`set-all-art-level`, `set-all-art-max`). Individual art tuning and even *seeing* per-art values requires reading hex.

## Proposal

- `get-art <index>` / `set-art <index> <level>` / `set-art-max <index> <max>` (subcommands)
- `list-arts`: table of all 188 arts (index, name, level, unlock tier)
- Build an art name/index table (character → arts, including talent arts). The 188-entry layout needs mapping against the XCDESave C# library arts enumeration; verify order on a real save (e.g. Shulk's Monado arts first)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `list-arts` prints all arts with names and current values
- [ ] Single-art set/get with bounds validation
- [ ] Art name table verified against a real save
- [ ] Unit tests with fabricated saves

title: Route library prints through logging to silence test output noise
description:
## Problem

Library code prints directly ("Backup created at ...", "Save file written to ..."), so `python -m unittest` output is polluted with unrelated lines (see test run logs). Printing inside library methods also makes future embedding (JSON export, interactive mode) awkward.

## Fix

- Route library messages through the `logging` module (`logger.info`)
- Keep CLI-visible output by configuring a console handler in `main()`, or have `save()` return the message and let the CLI print it

title: Add restore-backup command
description:
## Target

`restore-backup <save>`: copy `<save>.backup` back over `<save>` (atomically), refusing if no backup exists. Optionally keep a `.pre-restore` copy of the current file before overwriting.

## Value

Backups are created automatically but restoring is currently a manual copy; pairing with `--in-place` makes the edit cycle safe and round-trippable.

title: Add set-all-ap / set-all-xp batch commands
description:
## Background

`set-all-level` exists but there is no batch equivalent for AP/XP. Setting 15 characters one-by-one is tedious, and the planned `max-out` command builds on this.

## Proposal

- `set-all-ap <value>` (alias `saa`): set AP for all characters 1-15
- `set-all-xp <value>` (alias `saxp`): set XP for all characters 1-15
- Same validation as the single-character variants

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both commands work via CLI with aliases
- [ ] Unit tests verify all 15 characters updated and validation errors propagate

title: Keep XP and level consistent (XP-per-level table + sync option)
description:
## Background

`set-xp` currently prints "Note: You may need to adjust the level separately". Level and XP are inconsistent after editing either one, and the game may behave oddly (level-ups triggering on next fight, etc.).

## Proposal

- Add a `--with-level` flag to `set-xp` (or a dedicated `set-level-auto` command): when setting level N, also set XP to the game's canonical XP requirement for N
- Build the level→XP table: derive from in-game values (XP needed for each level 1-99); store as a constant table in the module
- Alternatively `set-level <id> <level> --sync-xp` sets both consistently

## Notes

- The exact XP-per-level table needs to be sourced (game data / wikis) and spot-checked against real saves
- Keep pure level-only edits working as today

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Consistent level+XP editing available via one command/flag
- [ ] XP table documented and spot-checked
- [ ] Unit tests
